bib.title: A Systematic Evaluation of Large Language Models of Code

question: How do existing large code LMs (Codex, GPT-Neo/J/NeoX, CodeParrot) compare, and how does an open code-only multilingual model trained from scratch fare?
hypothesis: Multilingual code LMs may generalise across languages and outperform monolingual ones (stated as yet to be verified).
contributions: Systematic comparison of Codex, GPT-Neo, GPT-J, GPT-NeoX and CodeParrot on HumanEval and per-language perplexity
Release of PolyCoder (160M, 400M, 2.7B), open-source, trained on 12 programming languages

method.summary: Trains three GPT-2-architecture models on 253.6GB of filtered GitHub code in 12 languages and evaluates them with existing models on HumanEval (Pass@k) and on per-language perplexity over unseen GitHub files.
method.task: code LM pretraining; NL-to-Python synthesis; per-language perplexity

datasets.name: PolyCoder GitHub corpus
datasets.size: 253.6G, 24,082,681 files after filtering (631.4G raw, 147,095 repos in Table 1)
datasets.source: GitHub repos with at least 50 stars, up to about 25K per language, cloned October 2021
datasets.preprocessing: drop files >1MB or <100 tokens (631GB to 424GB), exact hash dedup; no auto-generated-file filter

datasets.name: Unseen GitHub perplexity set
datasets.source: GitHub repos not in the Pile's GitHub portion
datasets.preprocessing: log-likelihood sum normalised by Pygments token count

models.name: PolyCoder 2.7B
models.tokenizer: GPT-2 BPE tokenizer trained on random 5% of pretraining data, all languages

other.note: GPT-NeoX not run on HumanEval for cost

training.objective: inferred: left-to-right next-token prediction (GPT-2 style LM); not stated explicitly
training.lr_schedule: Cosine decay; decay adjusted to half the default 320K steps

other.note: validation loss still decreasing at 150K, authors say models under-fit

metrics.name: Pass@1, Pass@10, Pass@100
metrics.definition: HumanEval functional correctness with unit tests, from 100 samples

metrics.name: Perplexity
metrics.definition: per-language on unseen files; log-likelihood sum normalised by Pygments token count to compare across tokenizers

eval.protocol: Single run per setting; no seeds or significance tests stated. Best temperature chosen per metric.

evidence.where: Table 3: PolyCoder column shows a dash

results.claim: PolyCoder 2.7B reaches Pass@1 of 5.59% on HumanEval, below GPT-Neo 2.7B (6.41%) and GPT-J 6B (11.62%).
results.setup: HumanEval (164 prompts), best over T in {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8}, top-p 0.95, 100 samples per prompt

results.claim: Codex 12B is far ahead of all open models on HumanEval Pass@1.
results.setup: HumanEval (164 prompts), best over T in {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8}, top-p 0.95, 100 samples per prompt; Codex via API
results.note: baseline is GPT-J 6B, best open model

results.setup: HumanEval (164 prompts), best over T in {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8}, top-p 0.95, 100 samples per prompt
HumanEval (164 prompts), best over T in {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8}, top-p 0.95, 100 samples per prompt

results.claim: PolyCoder beats CodeParrot 1.5B on Pass@1 (5.59 vs 3.58).
results.setup: HumanEval (164 prompts), best over T in {0.2,0.4,0.6,0.8}, top-p 0.95, 100 samples per prompt; CodeParrot 1.5B, trained on Python only

results.claim: PolyCoder 2.7B has seen only 2.5B Python tokens, far fewer than GPT-Neo 2.7B (4.3B) and CodeParrot (26B); authors offer this as partial explanation of the HumanEval gap.
results.table: Table 4, row PolyCoder (2.7B), column Python Tokens

results.claim: PolyCoder 2.7B gets lowest perplexity of all models in C, including Codex.
results.setup: 100 random unseen GitHub files per language; Codex (code-davinci-001) may have seen the test files

results.claim: Codex perplexity in Python is much lower than PolyCoder's.
results.setup: Python eval files; Codex possibly contaminated

results.claim: CodeParrot, trained only on Python, has very high perplexity on other languages (19.23 in C).
PolyCoder 2.7B beats GPT-Neo 2.7B in C, JavaScript, Rust, Scala and TypeScript perplexity.
results.quote: Comparing the open-source models only, PolyCoder performs better than the similarly sized GPT-Neo 2.7B in C, JavaScript, Rust, Scala and TypeScript.

results.claim: Python perplexity ranking tracks HumanEval ranking, so perplexity is proposed as a cheap proxy.
results.quote: This suggests that perplexity is a useful and low-cost metric to estimate other, downstream, metrics.

results.claim: Pass@1 favours low temperature, Pass@100 higher temperature, Pass@10 in the middle; T=0.8 hurts the 2.7B model at Pass@100.
results.quote: The general trend is for Pass@1, lower temperatures are better, and for Pass@100, a higher temperature will help, while for Pass@10 a temperature in the middle is better suited.

results.claim: HumanEval performance rises roughly linearly with log parameter count for Codex, PolyCoder and GPT-Neo/J; CodeParrot saturates.
results.quote: The performance on HumanEval benchmark increases linearly with the magnitude (log scale) of the number of parameters in the model.

results.claim: Training 2.7B model from 100K to 150K steps improves Pass@k uniformly, most at Pass@100; the 400M model gains little and Pass@100 drops.
results.quote: We can see that in the larger 2.7B model, by training the model longer till 150K steps, the performance increases uniformly, with Pass@100 increasing the most.

results.claim: Cleaned corpus is 253.6G across 24,082,681 files after filtering and dedup (631.4G raw per Table 1).
results.note: Abstract says 249GB; text says 254GB; Table 1 says 253.6G; text says unfiltered 631GB and 38.9M files
results.table: Table 1, row Total, column Size After Filtering

results.claim: Size filtering and dedup reduced file count by 38% and dataset size by 61%.
results.setup: filter >1MB and <100 tokens, then exact hash dedup
results.quote: reduced the number of files by 38%, and the dataset size by 61%

results.claim: Training the 2.7B model took about 6 weeks on 8 RTX 8000 GPUs.
results.setup: 8 Nvidia RTX 8000, single machine, GPT-NeoX toolkit
results.quote: The wall time used to train the largest 2.7B model is about 6 weeks.

limits: No hyperparameter search because of cost.
2.7B model under-trained: 150K steps with decay shortened from 320K; validation loss still falling.
Codex training data unknown, so perplexity results may be contaminated (over-optimistic).
HumanEval is Python only; other languages measured by perplexity only.
Best-temperature selection per metric on the test benchmark.
Explanations (value of natural-language text, language imbalance) are hypotheses, not tested by ablation.
Single runs; no seeds or variance.
Dated: Codex-era models; superseded by later open code models.
